title: Cagrilintide side effects: how often each one happened in the trials
excerpt: The main cagrilintide side effects in trials were nausea, constipation and other stomach effects, in 41% to 63% of people on cagrilintide alone against 32% on placebo [[1]], plus injection-site reactions. Here is each rate, trial by trial.
body:
The most common cagrilintide side effects in clinical trials were gastrointestinal: nausea, constipation and diarrhoea. In the phase 2 trial of cagrilintide alone, 41% to 63% of participants on the drug had a gastrointestinal adverse event, depending on dose, against 32% on placebo, and nausea affected 20% to 47% against 18% [[1]]. Injection-site (administration-site) reactions were among the most frequent events too [[1]]. Most stomach effects in the larger phase 3 trials were mild to moderate and transient [[2]].

This page sets out each rate from the trials that reported it, compares cagrilintide with semaglutide and placebo in the same trials, and says what is still unknown. It belongs to the guide on how cagrilintide works; the trial doses behind these numbers are in cagrilintide dosage in the trials, and the combination product has its own record, CagriSema.

Two things stand out. Cagrilintide alone produces fewer stomach effects than the combination, but more than placebo, and the gap rises with dose. And the combination's stomach effects in phase 3 run at roughly twice the placebo rate, which is the usual pattern for drugs in this group.

sections.heading: Nausea, constipation and other stomach effects
sections.html:
Nausea is the signature side effect. In phase 2 its rate climbed with the dose, from 20% at the lowest cagrilintide dose to 47% at the highest, against 18% on placebo [[1]]. Constipation and diarrhoea were the other common gastrointestinal events in that trial [[1]]. In REDEFINE 1, nausea affected 55% on CagriSema against 12.6% on placebo, constipation 30.7% against 11.6%, and vomiting 26.1% against 4.1% [[5]].

The reason is mechanistic. Amylin slows gastric emptying and acts on brainstem areas that control appetite [[8]], and cagrilintide works partly through the area postrema [[9]], the brainstem region that also triggers nausea. That is one reason Eli Lilly built eloralintide to be more selective: in rats it produced less conditioned taste avoidance than cagrilintide [[10]]. The broader comparison of these drugs is in amylin analogs.

sections.heading: Injection-site reactions
sections.html: The phase 2 monotherapy trial listed administration-site reactions alongside gastrointestinal disorders as the most frequent adverse events with cagrilintide [[1]]. The published abstract does not give a rate for them, and the phase 3 publications summarised here do not report injection-site rates for cagrilintide alone. So the evidence supports saying these reactions were common in phase 2, not putting a number on them. Figures quoted elsewhere without a trial name should be treated with caution. Injection technique and site rotation are covered in subcutaneous injection sites.

sections.heading: Cagrilintide side effects compared with semaglutide and placebo
sections.lede: The fairest comparisons come from trials that ran all the arms at once.
sections.html:
Any adverse event in REIMAGINE 2, by arm, 68 weeks
ArmParticipants with any adverse event
CagriSema, 2.4 mg of each86.9% (524 of 603) [[3]]
Cagrilintide 2.4 mg alone82.2% (125 of 152) [[3]]
Semaglutide 2.4 mg alone81.2% (491 of 605) [[3]]
CagriSema, 1.0 mg of each81.6% (485 of 594) [[3]]
Semaglutide 1.0 mg alone78.5% (477 of 608) [[3]]
Placebo70.5% (105 of 149) [[3]]

In that trial, in adults with type 2 diabetes, cagrilintide alone and semaglutide alone produced almost the same overall rate of adverse events, and gastrointestinal disorders were the most common in every active group [[3]]. In the smaller phase 2 diabetes trial the figures were 80% on cagrilintide, 71% on semaglutide and 68% on CagriSema [[4]], numbers too small to rank them.

Adding cagrilintide to semaglutide raises the rate modestly. In REDEFINE 5, gastrointestinal events affected 53% on CagriSema against 51% on semaglutide alone, while 10% stopped CagriSema against 6% who stopped semaglutide [[7]]. Pooled analyses put this in context: one 2026 meta-analysis found adverse events more frequent with cagrilintide or CagriSema than placebo but discontinuation rates comparable to placebo [[11]], and a network meta-analysis found that only high-dose CagriSema increased discontinuation for adverse events [[12]]. The head-to-head arms are compared in full in cagrilintide vs semaglutide.

sections.heading: When cagrilintide side effects happen
sections.html:
The trials describe gastrointestinal effects as mainly transient and mild to moderate [[2]][[6]]. They cluster during the period when the amount is being raised, which is why every trial escalated gradually: the phase 2 trial used a dose-escalation period of up to 6 weeks [[1]], and the phase 1b trial co-escalated cagrilintide and semaglutide in 4-week steps over 16 weeks [[13]]. Those schedules are reported here as what the trials administered, not as a plan for anyone; they are tabulated in cagrilintide dosage.

Because cagrilintide has a half-life of 159 to 195 hours [[13]], an effect that starts after an injection can take days to fade. The published abstracts do not give a week-by-week curve of side effects for cagrilintide alone.

sections.heading: Serious adverse events and dedicated safety studies
sections.html:
• Heart rhythm. A thorough QT study in 105 healthy adults, with 53 escalated to 4.5 mg of cagrilintide, found no clinically relevant QTc prolongation [[14]].
  • Kidney and liver. In dedicated studies, kidney or liver impairment produced no increase in adverse events and no new safety findings [[15]].
  • Low blood sugar. In the phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes, no level 2 or level 3 hypoglycaemia and no fatal adverse events were reported [[4]].
  • Deaths. REDEFINE 5 reported one death, in the semaglutide group, judged unrelated to treatment [[7]].
  • Class pattern. REIMAGINE 2 described the CagriSema safety profile as consistent with the GLP-1 receptor agonist class and previous cagrilintide data [[3]].

sections.heading: What is not known about cagrilintide safety
sections.html:
• Long-term use. The longest completed trials ran 68 weeks for weight loss [[2]]. The CagriSema cardiovascular-outcomes trial, REDEFINE 3, is still running [[5]].
  • Cagrilintide alone in phase 3. The dedicated RENEW trials have started but not reported [[16]].
  • Rare events. Trials of a few thousand people can miss uncommon harms; no regulator has yet reviewed the full safety file and published a label [[5]].
  • Products outside trials. Every number on this page describes the manufacturer's drug in monitored trials. For anything sold under the name, identity, purity and dose are unknown, which adds risks no trial measured.

faq.question: What are the side effects of cagrilintide?
faq.answer: Mainly nausea, constipation and diarrhoea, plus injection-site reactions. In phase 2, gastrointestinal events affected 41% to 63% on cagrilintide against 32% on placebo [[1]].

faq.question: Does cagrilintide cause less nausea than semaglutide?
faq.answer: Not clearly. In REIMAGINE 2, overall adverse events were 82.2% on cagrilintide alone and 81.2% on semaglutide alone [[3]]. No trial abstract reports a nausea rate for each drug alone side by side.

faq.question: Do cagrilintide side effects go away?
faq.answer: In the phase 3 trials the stomach effects were mainly transient and mild to moderate [[2]][[6]].

faq.question: How many people stopped cagrilintide because of side effects?
faq.answer: In phase 2, 4% of all participants stopped for adverse events, similar across groups [[1]]. In REDEFINE 1, 5.9% stopped CagriSema for adverse events against 3.5% on placebo [[5]].
